author: John Neff
title: Akre Focus ETF Second Quarter 2026 Commentary
headline: Akre is down 24% over a year as AI hardware soars. The team sees its software and payments holdings at a decade-low 17x free cash flow.
summary: The Akre Focus ETF gained 0.66% in the second quarter against 15.20% for the S&P 500 and lost 24.01% over twelve months. The team says its companies keep growing: free cash flow per share rose 23% in the first quarter, and the portfolio trades at just over 17 times free cash flow, the lowest since 2016. Around AI it sees classic signs of speculation: semiconductors at about 20% of the S&P 500, record margin debt and leveraged ETFs, and SpaceX valued at nearly 120 times annualised revenue. The market brands its software and information-services holdings as AI victims; Akre argues they are adopting AI and stays “lashed to the mast”.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: The fund looks stronger and cheaper than at any point in ten years: projected free-cash-flow-per-share growth near 16% a year, a free-cash-flow return on capital of about 42% and debt of 1.4 times EBITDA.

takeaways.label: View
takeaways.text: AI can deliver on its promise and still destroy value for many investors, as railroads, cars and the internet did before.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: AI labs’ moats: among OpenRouter users, the share of tokens going to Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini fell from 72% to 33% in a year as users moved to cheaper open-source models.

takeaways.label: Watch
takeaways.text: Memory: new Chinese capacity from CXMT and Yangtze Memory could arrive as early as 2027 and end the shortage behind Micron’s and Sandisk’s surge.

takeaways.label: Move
takeaways.text: Cash fell from 4.4% to 1.7% of net assets during the quarter.

risks.text: Speculation is spreading: record retail trading, about $218 billion in leveraged ETFs and $1.4 trillion of margin debt.
AI model makers lack switching costs and pricing power; Anthropic has revenue comparable to Mastercard’s but no net profit.
If AI causes mass job losses, resource shortages or inflation, politicians may respond in ways that undercut the AI leaders’ growth.

quotes.text: What keeps history rhyming is not faulty foundations, but the towering speculative excesses built on top of them that eventually collapse.
We do not see our portfolio companies stalled on the tracks of an oncoming AI train.
We remain securely lashed to the mast of our process and convictions, bound by our focus on the strong fundamentals and attractive valuations of our portfolio companies.

stocks.note: Largest holding (13.9%); its tokenisation will matter for AI-driven commerce.
No material customer losses to AI-native start-ups across about 1,500 businesses.
Has filed 137 AI-based patents; a top-five contributor.
Rated over $100 billion of AI-related debt in the first quarter.
Agentforce and Data 360 revenue run rate up 225% to $3.4 billion; still a detractor.
Raised its 2026 AI revenue guidance by 50%.
Emerging Solutions revenue +50%, with AI the largest part.
Detractor; launched AI search on Homes.com and Apartments.com.
Among the bottom five performers in the quarter.
A sign of speculation to Akre: valued at nearly 120 times annualised revenue after its June IPO.
